title: Fake helpline found online asks for PIN vs. genuine helpline raises a dispute
summary: The recipient notices a debit on their Kaveri Bank card that they do not recognise and phones "customer care". In the fraud case, the recipient dialled a number found through a web search. The agent who answers asks for the full card number, CVV, and ATM PIN to "raise the dispute". In the legitimate case, the recipient dialled the number printed on the back of the card. The agent checks identity using non-secret details, blocks the card, and raises a dispute with a ticket number. Both agents ask verification questions.

shared_setting.pretext: an unrecognised card debit of [AMOUNT_1] (₹1,000–₹20,000) at an online merchant.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank customer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both agents answer as "Kaveri Bank customer care", give a name, and say they will "verify a few details" first.

fraud.label_rationale: The agent asks the recipient to disclose secret card credentials (CVV and ATM PIN). No bank asks for these, including when a customer calls in.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the full card number, expiry, CVV, and PIN.
stable_facts: The recipient dialled [PHONE_1], a ten-digit mobile number shown in a web search result. This is setting context only, not evidence.
The agent sounds professional and uses a scripted greeting.
The agent says a "dispute form" must be filled in on the call.

caller_continuation_limits: (In this inbound family the "caller" role is the helpline agent.) The fraud agent may repeat the request, claim the dispute will be rejected without it, or give up. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example a screen-sharing install or payment request). The legitimate agent must not ask for any PIN, CVV, OTP, or full card number after the branch.

must_preserve: debit amount and last-four in both
non-secret verification, block, ticket, and explicit "never PIN/CVV/OTP" (_L)
may_vary: how the recipient found the number (mentioned or not in dialogue)
up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real search engine or bank names

ambiguities: Both agents "verify details". The label depends on which details: secret credentials versus non-secret ones.
Where the recipient got the number is setting context. The generator may let the recipient mention it, but the label must not rest on it.
A genuine helpline may ask for date of birth or registered mobile. These are not secret credentials and must not be treated as evidence of fraud.
Cross-domain overlap: ec_09 (fake support number for a marketplace, card details asked) is the same mechanism. Deduplication should keep one or vary them clearly.

evidence_references.claim: Contact numbers on search engines may be fraudulent (C07)
Imposters on search-result numbers ask callers for card credentials; customer care numbers are never mobile numbers (CB12)
Banks never ask for PIN, CVV, OTP, or passwords (C01)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
